subject: Performance & latency benchmarking review - scheduling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Joe Smith <joe.smith@acme.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Performance & latency benchmarking review - scheduling

Hi Joe —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We'd like to set up a technical deep-dive / architecture review focused on performance and latency benchmarking for the integration (load tests, token throughput targets, and observability).

Proposed agenda (30–45min):
- Test objectives and success criteria (throughput/latency targets)
- Test matrix: model variants, sequence lengths, concurrency
- Test harness and monitoring hooks (metrics we will collect)
- Roles: who runs tests, who provides data/service accounts
- Next steps & timeline

We have availability on:
- Fri Mar 12: 9:00–11:00 AM PT
- Mon Mar 15: 10:00–12:00 PM PT

Please let me know what works for you and who from your side will join (engineering/infra). I attached a short benchmark plan and a preliminary test matrix to help prep.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0148

From: Joe Smith <joe.smith@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance & latency benchmarking review - scheduling

Marissa —

Thanks for the note. Can we move this to Mon Mar 15? I'll be traveling on Friday.

Proposed participants from Acme: myself (Platform), Elena Park (Engineering Lead), and our SRE (TBD). 11:00 AM PT on Mar 15 would be ideal for us.

High-level targets we want to validate during the session (so you can prepare):
- Sustained token throughput target: ~10,000 tokens/min (~167 tokens/sec) for batched requests
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 512-token sequences (cold vs warm cache behavior)
- Desired load test durations: 20–30 minutes per configuration (plus warm-up)

Would you be able to confirm which test harness you plan to use and whether you need a service account from us?

Best,
Joe Smith
VP, Platform Engineering | Acme.ai
joe.smith@acme.ai

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance & latency benchmarking review - scheduling

Joe —

Mar 15 at 11:00 AM PT works for our team. I've added Dev and Olga from our infra/perf teams — they'll run the load tests and instrument metrics on the Redwood side.

Agenda (finalized):
1) Objective & success criteria (confirm targets)
2) Test matrix walk-through (models, token lengths, concurrency)
3) Test harness & run plan (warm-up, steady-state, durations)
4) Observability & tracing (what metrics/logs we'll collect)
5) Next steps (actions and owners)

We plan to test the following configurations (high-level):
- Model variants: open-llm-1.0 (float16), open-llm-1.0-quant (8-bit)
- Sequence lengths: 128 / 512 / 1024 tokens
- Concurrency: 1, 4, 8 simultaneous streams
- Batching: dynamic batching up to 16 requests

Run plan suggestion: warm-up 10 minutes, then 25 minutes steady-state per config. We'll capture token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.

Attachments: load_test_matrix.csv
Calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-acme-benchmark-20260315
Docs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/benchmark-plan

See you Monday.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Joe Smith <joe.smith@acme.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance & latency benchmarking review - scheduling (test prerequisites)

Joe / Marissa —

A few prerequisites and clarifications from the test-run side so we can hit the targets you've outlined:

What we need from Acme:
- Sample prompt set (representative distribution) and expected prompt mix (percent chat vs. batch requests)
- Expected QPS spike profile (steady qps vs bursty patterns)
- Service account/key with permission to call your test endpoint or a test dataset for us to drive client-side load if you prefer to run tests from your side

Test harness & recommendations:
- We'll use the Redwood load harness (k6 wrapper + custom adapter) and emit metrics to Prometheus + Grafana dashboards.
- Suggested run: warm-up 10m, steady 30m per config for stable percentiles.
- We'll instrument token-level timing (generation step) and end-to-end request latency.
- For throughput targets: we'll validate both per-GPU and cluster-level throughput; please confirm whether you want us to run from us-east1 / us-west1 or you will run from your infra.

Operational notes:
- Please share any IP allowlist / firewall rules for the service-account IPs we should use.
- If you have rate-limiting rules in front of your endpoints, let us know expected limits so we can avoid false throttling.

Attn: Olga — we'll coordinate on traces and kernel-level counters (GPU SM + memory) during the run.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
From: Joe Smith <joe.smith@acme.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acme.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance & latency benchmarking review - scheduling (test prerequisites)

Thanks, Dev —

I've uploaded a zipped sample prompt set to our shared drive (link below) and flagged the prompt mix: 70% short chat prompts (~50–150 tokens), 30% long generation (~400–800 tokens). We can provision a service account for Redwood or run the harness from our side — we prefer Redwood-run tests from us-east1 to minimize network variance, but we can also run a client-side pass if helpful.

Shared files: https://drive.acme.ai/teams/platform/benchmark-samples
Attachment: acme_prompt_samples.zip

Also looping in Elena so she can confirm the SRE contact and firewall rules. We'll aim to have a service account ready by Monday morning.

Cheers,
Joe
